title: LumenBridge kiosk voicebot field notes
body:
Quick capture from discovery + field call with LumenBridge (3/4/26). Rough raw notes — not customer-facing.

Attendees:
- LumenBridge: Sarah Cho (PM), Tomasz Kowalski (SRE), Neha Iyer (QA lead)
- Redwood: Priya Nair (SE, owner), Marco Ruiz (infra), Aisha Patel (privacy)

Goal: understand constraints for a retail self-service kiosk voice assistant prototype (pilot of 50 devices) and map Redwood deployment options + immediate integration risks.

Summary: customer wants a low-latency, mostly-offline voice assistant for checkout help and info lookup. Devices run Linux on NXP i.MX8 or Jetson Nano-class hw (mixed fleet). Network: intermittent 4G/5G at stores, some sites with reliable wired LAN. They will try on-device small model for wake/slot-filling and fall back to Redwood-hosted inference for complex queries. Expectation: sub-400ms median for local responses; <1.5s acceptable for cloud fallback. Data must not leave customer VPC for PII cases; need auditability and ability to opt-out sending transcripts.

Key tech constraints / non-negotiables:
- Must support offline-first mode: local on-device inference for small NLU tasks.
- Any cloud calls with customer data must be routed through Private deployment (VPC) or Dedicated nodes with explicit routing rules.
- PII scrub/PII classification must run locally before sending upstream. Customer will supply their PII patterns / regexes.
- Devices have only 4 GB usable GPU/accelerator memory (Jetson Nano variant), so large fp16 models are out unless quantized.
- Wake-word and VAD must run with <50ms additional CPU overhead; cannot block user experience.

Integration pieces discussed:
- Local runtime: embed our lightweight runtime container + minimal model (intent classification + slot extraction). Options: quantized 8-bit or int4 trimmed model. Need guidance from Redwood research on quantization profile for NLU models.
- Cloud fallback: Redwood Private control plane in their AWS account (VPC endpoint). We'll recommend dedicated nodes in the same region (us-east-1).
- KV/prefix cache: use local state on device for common prompts (store last 10 queries + cached responses).
- Authentication: device TLS mutual auth + device identity via customer-managed PKI (they prefer HSM-stored keys).

Performance and cost considerations:
- They care about consistent latency (SLO) over raw throughput. For cloud fallback, propose Dedicated capacity with SLOs.
- For on-device, we should give them a quantization/retraining plan: start with 6B->4B quantized intent model, measure local latency.
- Batching on cloud side not helpful for sub-second single-user flows; recommend minimal batching and focus on model selection instead.

Security & compliance notes:
- Data retention: logs must be retained in their account for 90 days by default; audit logs forwarded to their SIEM (Splunk).
- PII opt-out toggle: customer must be able to mark specific utterances as "no upload" at runtime. Redwood-side policy needs to honour attribute in request metadata.
- On-device encryption at rest required for cached transcripts.

Gotchas / risk areas:
- Audio sampling mismatch: some kiosks send 8kHz narrowband; our NLU models now assume 16kHz. Need to confirm preprocessing on device or a small resampler library to avoid accuracy regressions.
- Wake-word false positives in noisy environments — they want a configurable threshold. Must instrument metrics in Redwood Console for true positive rate.
- Model drift: kiosk vocabulary is retail-specific (SKUs, local slang). They will provide initial lexicon; we need an easy pipeline to add domain-specific tokens and deploy a patched model.
- Edge fleet heterogeneity: two HW families means two quantization calibration sets. This increases effort.
- Offline logs: when devices come back online, they will upload batched transcripts. Must ensure watermarking to prevent duplication.

Proposed short-term approach (MVP):
1) Tech spike (2 weeks): run quantized intent model on device images (Jetson Nano emulator) to measure latency & accuracy. Owner: Marco Ruiz (SE). Jira: LUM-78-1
2) Private control plane PoC (3 weeks): deploy Redwood Private in their AWS sandbox, configure VPC endpoint and device mutual-TLS. Owner: Priya Nair. Jira: LUM-78-2
3) Privacy filter: ship a tiny local PII-scrubber lib (Python/C++) and add metadata flag for "no-upload". Owner: Aisha Patel. Jira: LUM-78-3
4) Field trial (6 weeks): 10 kiosks in two stores, measure latency, false wake rate, and fallback ratio. Collect sample transcripts for eval. Owner: LumenBridge ops + Redwood SRE.

Instrumentation / telemetry to capture:
- wake_word_trigger_rate, wake_false_positive_rate, local_inference_latency_p50/p90/p99, cloud_fallback_latency_p50/p90, fallback_ratio, bytes_sent_per_day_per_device, downstream_cost_estimate_per_device.
- Need per-device token-level cost export to their billing account. Redwood Console should allow per-device tags.

Open questions (action items):
- Customer to confirm exact HW SKU list and whether Jetson Xavier NX is in scope. (Action: Sarah)
- Confirm audio format(s) from firmware (16kHz PCM or 8kHz compressed). (Action: Tomasz)
- Agree on PII patterns and sample data for scrubbing tests (Action: Neha)
- Do they want a restful polling model for batched upload or streaming? They prefer small batch upload for offline mode. Need Redwood guidance on watermarking. (Action: Priya)

Next steps / immediate owners: 
- Priya: circulate this note + proposed PoC plan to LumenBridge; schedule spike kickoff next Tue (3/9).
- Marco: prepare Jetson Nano test runner + initial quantization script by 3/11.
- Aisha: draft PII scrub checklist and example regex set by 3/12.
- LumenBridge (Sarah): share firmware audio format and device SKUs by 3/9.

Decisions to surface for product/PD:
- We should add a small-device quantization guide to Optimize docs (how to pick bit-width, perf tradeoffs).
- Consider adding a device-level "no-upload" metadata flag as a first-class SDK feature in next minor release (v0.9.x).

Misc notes / random thoughts:
- Could try an ultra-small on-device LLM for clarification prompts (e.g., 100M param distilled model) to avoid cloud trips for simple disambiguation. Might be feasible with heavy quantization. Research to evaluate.
- If they need voice synthesis (TTS) later, recommend local TTS with caching; cloud TTS will blow up cost.

Raw transcript snippets (for evaluation) - ask for permission to copy to Redwood evals repo: 
- "Where is aisle twelve?" -> intent: locate-product, slot: aisle=12
- "I need to return this item, it's broken" -> intent: return-initiate

Notes for follow-up meeting: agenda: show Jetson spike results, confirm Private sandbox deployment, demo PII scrub with sample audio.

---

Internal: tag as high-touch potential enterprise (Dedicated/Private upsell). Keep sales loop informed after PoC success.

End of notes.
